title: Second Reading of the National Council of Social Service (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to amend the National Council of Social Service Act, moved by the Minister for Social and Family Development, updating NCSS's objectives, membership, Council governance and related statutory provisions.
why_it_matters: The Bill updates NCSS's statutory objectives and functions to strengthen social service delivery, build sector capabilities and develop the broader social service ecosystem. It introduces a single-tier sector membership and a fully appointed Council, and extends ComChest's role beyond fundraising. The record says these changes are intended to improve outcomes for service users and support those in need.

key_points.point: The Minister moved that the Bill be now read a Second time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: That the Bill be now read a Second time.

key_points.point: The Bill refreshes NCSS's objectives, functions and powers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: The first key area relates to refreshing NCSS' objectives, functions and powers.

key_points.point: NCSS's core objectives are strengthening social service delivery, building sector stakeholders' capability and developing the broader social service ecosystem.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: First, strengthening social service delivery. Second, building the capability of sector stakeholders. And third, developing the broader social service ecosystem.

key_points.point: Clause 6 inserts new sections 11 and 12 on the Council's objectives, functions and powers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: Clause 6 reflects this by inserting a new section 11 on objectives and functions of Council and section 12 on powers of Council.

key_points.point: NCSS will monitor service users' progress and make data available to the sector.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: NCSS will monitor service users' progress and make data available to the sector.

key_points.point: Clause 10 introduces a single-tier sector membership framework.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: clause 10 introduces sector membership, a single-tier membership framework for organisations in the sector to complement NCSS' sector developer role.

key_points.point: No fees will be charged for sector membership.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: However, fees will not be charged for sector membership.

key_points.point: All Full Council members will transition to become sector members.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: All Full Council members, who make up the majority of NCSS' membership today, will be transitioned to become sector members.

key_points.point: At least half of the Council, excluding the Chairperson, will be appointed from individuals nominated by sector members.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: at least half of the Council, excluding the Chairperson, will be appointed from individuals nominated by sector members.

key_points.point: The Council will have a maximum of 27 members, a minimum of 15, and a maximum term of three years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: The Council will comprise a maximum of 27 members and a minimum of 15, with a maximum term of three years.

key_points.point: Clause 7 extends ComChest's role beyond fundraising to mobilising other resources such as volunteers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: Clause 7 provides that ComChest's role extends beyond fundraising to include mobilising other resources, such as volunteers.

key_points.point: The Bill reclassifies NCSS as a Group 1A public body in the First Schedule to the Public Sector (Governance) Act 2018.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: reclassifying NCSS as a Group 1A public body in the First Schedule to the Public Sector (Governance) Act 2018

key_points.point: MSF funding for social service programmes doubled from $172 million in FY2014 to $346 million in FY2024.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: MSF's funding for social service programmes has doubled in the last decade from $172 million dollars in financial year (FY)2014 to $346 million dollars in FY2024.

key_points.point: Mr Xie Yao Quan declared an interest and supported the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
key_points.quote: I stand in support of this Bill.

key_points.point: Prof Kenneth Poon asked for clarification on the rationale for the wider Council size range of 15 to 27.
key_points.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon
key_points.quote: I would appreciate some clarification on the rationale for providing this wider range.

key_points.point: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng raised the risk of over-centralisation.
key_points.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
key_points.quote: Concern number one: risk of over-centralisation.

key_points.point: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng asked how compliance and reporting requirements will be calibrated to the size, capacity and maturity of SSAs.
key_points.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
key_points.quote: How will compliance and reporting requirements be calibrated to the size, to the capacity and maturity of the SSAs in this sector

key_points.point: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim supported the Bill and its intentions.
key_points.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
key_points.quote: I support the Bill and its intentions.

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal said a sector cannot be sustainable if its workforce is not.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: A sector cannot be sustainable if its workforce is not.

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal asked whether the first quarter of 2026 remains the intended timeline for wage-guideline harmonisation.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: Could the Minister confirm whether the first quarter in 2026 remains the intended timeline for wage-guideline harmonisation

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye supported removing membership fees and streamlining to a single-tier membership framework.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: I fully support the proposal to remove membership fees and to streamline to a single-tier membership framework.

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye asked for the reasons behind setting a large maximum Council size.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
key_points.quote: what were the reasons behind setting such a large maximum size of the Council?

key_points.point: Ms Elysa Chen asked for clarity on how public interest is distinguished from administrative convenience.
key_points.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
key_points.quote: We need clarity on how public interest is distinguished from administrative convenience.

key_points.point: The Minister said about 400 Full Council Members and close to 100 Associate Council Members exist today.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: Today, there are about 400 Full Council Members and close to 100 Associate Council Members.

key_points.point: The Minister said Associate Council membership will be ceased.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: Associate Council membership will be ceased.

key_points.point: The Minister said appeals will go to the Minister only if an applicant disputes a decision that the Council stands by.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: Appeals will only go to the Minister if an applicant disputes a decision that the Council stands by.

key_points.point: The Minister said an appointment approach gives greater certainty that the Council can be constituted with people from various backgrounds.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: an appointment approach gives us greater certainty that we can constitute the Council with people from various backgrounds

key_points.point: The Minister said current NCSS Board and committee members are intended to serve out their current term until 31 July 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: our intent is for them to serve out their current term, that is, until 31 July 2026.

key_points.point: The Minister said the amendments do not change ComChest's fundraising function.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: the amendments do not change the fundraising function of ComChest.

key_points.point: The Minister said MSF and NCSS will work with stakeholders including unions and MOH to ensure quality jobs and clear salary guidelines.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: we will work with all stakeholders, including sector members, unions and MOH to ensure there are quality jobs and clear salary guidelines in the sector.

key_points.point: The Minister said MSF and NCSS will set up a Protection Practitioners Care Fund.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: MSF and NCSS will be setting up a Protection Practitioners Care Fund

key_points.point: The Minister said NCSS first formally engaged the sector on the proposed amendments at its AGM in July 2024.
key_points.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
key_points.quote: NCSS first formally engaged the sector on the proposed amendments at its AGM in July 2024.

not_said: Whether the Bill was read a Second time or passed after the debate.
What specific criteria will be prescribed by Regulations for Council nominations and appointments.
How compliance and reporting requirements will be calibrated for smaller SSAs in practice.
Whether the first quarter 2026 timeline for wage-guideline harmonisation is confirmed.
How NCSS will coordinate with other agencies to identify and address service gaps.
What safeguards and due processes apply to sector membership decisions on public interest, public order or national harmony grounds.
Whether other administrative decisions, such as award and revocation of funds, will be open to formal appeals to the Minister.
How the transition for Associate Council members and affected organisations will work in practice.
What the composition of the Nominations Committee will be.
